events.text: Mid-form, something changes. A pale light runs along your blade and the practice post falls in two before you touch it. Sword aura.

effects.log: By morning you can call it at will, and your arms feel like someone else's.

choices.text: Put the sword down and think

effects.log: Power is a guest. You want to understand the host first.

events.text: Word of your realm has spread. Three young masters wait at the foot of your mountain, each hoping to make a name on you.

ok.log: You beat all three without drawing your full strength. One of them asks to become your disciple. You tell him to come back in ten years.

fail.log: The third one is better than the rumours said. You win, barely, and your ribs remind you for a month.

choices.text: Send them tea and a note

effects.log: The note says 'Train ten more years.' Two go home. One frames it.

events.text: Two orthodox sects are one insult away from war over a stolen well. Both sides ask you, and only you, to judge it.

effects.log: You rule for neither and make both dig a second well. The murim calls it the Well Judgement.
A fat purse, a thin peace. Everybody knows.

events.text: A letter written in blood: an old enemy from your youth has spent years training for one fight with you.

choices.text: Meet them at the appointed cliff

ok.log: Years of hatred, and it lasts eleven exchanges. Afterwards you share a pot of tea. Neither of you remembers what started it.

fail.log: They have trained well. You live, and so do they, and the grudge goes on.
fail.deathCause: an old enemy on the appointed cliff

effects.log: Years of hatred, answered with one honest page. They never come.

events.text: The great sects hold a banquet for the masters of the Transcendent realm. There are nine seats. One has your name on it.

effects.log: Nine masters, nine ways of seeing the same art. You learn more over one dinner than in a year of training.
You put out every candle in the hall with one breath. Impressive. Two of the masters now dislike you.

events.text: In seclusion, your own face appears across the room and lists every mistake you ever made. The heart demon has come.

ok.log: You agree with every word, and it has nothing left to say. It fades. Your mind is clearer than it has ever been.

fail.log: You argue with it for three days. You lose. Your meridians burn for a season.

choices.text: Break seclusion and walk it off

effects.log: Not today. The demon will wait. So will the next realm.

events.text: A great sect with no living master of your realm asks you to be its Guardian Elder: an honour, a room, and no duties except existing.

effects.log: Your name goes on their gate. Your fame spreads through their disciples.
You prefer to belong to nobody. The murim finds this very mysterious.

events.text: An old beggar watches you train and snorts. 'Too much sword. Not enough walking.' He is gone before you can ask what he means.

effects.log: You walk the length of the empire. When you return, your footwork has changed without you practising it.
Beggars say many things. Most of them are hungry.

events.text: A famine in the north. Your name could open the granaries of three rich sects, if you are willing to be rude to them.

effects.log: You are extraordinarily rude. The granaries open. Ten thousand people eat.
It costs a fortune. Nobody else has to lose face.

events.text: A young master you once gave pointers to has broken through to Peak Master. They come to thank you, nervous.

effects.log: They are good. You tell them so. They will remember this day longer than their breakthrough.

choices.text: Tell them the truth about the next gate

effects.log: It is harder than they think. You tell them how you nearly failed. It helps more than praise.

events.text: You learn that a guild of assassins has taken a contract on you. The price is flattering.

ok.log: You walk into their hall and sit down. They cancel the contract and return the deposit, somehow.

fail.log: You walk into their hall and nearly do not walk out. The contract stands.

effects.log: The first assassin arrives in spring. Your guards catch him. The guild quietly gives up.
You leave the city by night and spend the winter as nobody in a mountain village. By spring the contract has gone stale, and the guild has richer names to chase.

events.text: A famous poet wants to write an epic about your life. He needs to interview you for a month.

effects.log: He leaves out the funny parts and adds dragons. It becomes the most-sung song in the empire.

choices.text: Tell him about your first master instead

effects.log: That epic is better.

events.text: You cross an ancient battlefield where two legends fought a thousand years ago. The ground is still scarred with their sword aura.

ok.log: In the scars you see both of their styles, and why one of them lost. A thousand-year-old lesson.

fail.log: The old aura is still sharp. You leave with a cut and a headache.

effects.log: Some things are not yours to learn.

events.text: You sit on a mountain and, for the first time, cannot tell where your breath ends and the wind begins.

effects.log: A whole season passes like an afternoon. Your energy has no edges now.

choices.text: Come down before you forget your name

effects.log: Some masters stay up there forever. You still have noodles to eat.

events.text: The grandchildren of your old friends come to your door and bow as if you were a legend. In a way, you are.

effects.log: You lose at every game, deliberately. Their grandparents' laughter comes out of their mouths.
Just one. They will remember it when they are old.

events.text: The Emperor sends a golden edict: the court wishes to see a Harmony master with its own eyes.

effects.log: You drink tea with the Son of Heaven. He asks if you can fly. You say no. He looks disappointed and gives you a sword anyway.
The poem says the mountains are better company. The court argues about it for a year.

events.text: A dam upstream of three cities is cracking, and the rains have not stopped. Engineers say it will hold two days.

choices.text: Hold the dam with your energy while they drain it

ok.log: For a day and a night you stand in the flood and push. The water goes where it is told. Three cities never learn how close it was.

fail.log: You hold it, and it nearly holds you. You are carried out on a door, and it takes a year to walk straight.
fail.deathCause: the flood at the cracking dam

effects.log: Slower, safer, and everybody lives. The dam breaks into empty streets.

events.text: Rumours spread that you have found the elixir of youth. Half the rich men of the empire want to buy it.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: it is training

effects.log: They are very disappointed. Training is hard and cannot be bought.

choices.text: Sell them tea and let them believe

effects.log: It is very good tea. Nobody gets younger. You get richer.

events.text: The Demonic Cult sends an envoy with a black lotus: they would like a Harmony master as a friend, or at least not as an enemy.

effects.log: The Cult stays out of your region for ten years. The orthodox sects do not thank you for it.
Politely, burned. The envoy understands.

events.text: Another master of Harmony wants to know which of you is stronger. When Harmony masters duel, mountains change shape.

choices.text: Accept, at the top of Mount Hua

ok.log: Three days and three nights. On the fourth morning, your opponent laughs and bows. The peak is a little lower than it was.

fail.log: You lose by a hair. You shake hands on the broken summit and agree to do it again in ten years.
fail.deathCause: a duel of Harmony masters on Mount Hua

effects.log: Masters understand each other. You part as friends, and the rumour mills never forgive either of you.

events.text: A sect you have never visited is dying: no master, no money, twenty disciples. They send their eldest to ask a Harmony master what to do.

choices.text: Visit and teach for a season

effects.log: You stay one season and give them one good year. They carve your name on their gate.
Money helps. It does not teach anyone to breathe.

events.text: A dying monk presses a scrap of jade into your hand: 'Nine suns over nine mountains. You are the one who can read it.'

effects.log: A clue to the Primordial Scripture. (Seek the Primordial Scripture in the Jianghu to follow it.)

choices.text: Give it to the monk's temple

effects.log: Some treasures belong to the dead. The temple bows to you for a generation.

events.text: At your realm, fewer and fewer people understand anything you say about the martial way. It is a lonely height.

choices.text: Write letters to the other masters

effects.log: Three answer. One of them sends a riddle that takes you a year to solve.

choices.text: Talk to the children in the village instead

effects.log: They do not understand either, but they laugh at the right places.

events.text: Deep in the southern mountains lies a pool so cold it smokes. The locals say a dragon once slept here.

effects.log: The cold goes past your skin, past your bones, into your meridians. It is the best and worst hour of your life.
It stays cold in the gourd forever.

events.text: You realise you have not drawn your sword in three years, and nobody has dared to ask you to.

choices.text: Draw it once, for the joy of it

effects.log: The blade sings. A flock of birds leaves every tree for a mile. You laugh like a child.
A sword that is never drawn is the most frightening one of all.

events.text: Clouds gather over your mountain that have nothing to do with rain. Heaven has noticed you, and it is not pleased.

ok.log: Nine strikes. You stand through all of them. When the sky clears, your body is lighter, and your hair smells of smoke.

fail.log: The seventh strike puts you on your back. You live. Heaven will ask again.

choices.text: Go down into the valley and wait it out

effects.log: Heaven can wait. So can you.

events.text: Pilgrims camp outside your gate: a hundred young people, each hoping to be the one you take as a disciple.

choices.text: Take the one who swept the path every morning

effects.log: Not the strongest. Not the cleverest. The one who swept. Everybody learns something from it.
You send them home with rice and advice. The murim calls you the Closed Gate.

events.text: You have outlived everyone who fought you when you were young. You visit their graves, one by one.

effects.log: It takes a month. By the last grave you are not sure who won any of those fights, or why it mattered.

choices.text: Visit only the one you respected most

effects.log: You tell them about the realms beyond. You think they would have liked Mystic.

events.text: You look at a leaf and see its whole life: bud, green, gold, ground. Then you look at your hands.

effects.log: Everything is a leaf. It is not sad. It is very beautiful. (Walk through the Last Door in the Jianghu when you are ready.)
Enlightenment can wait until after lunch. That, too, is enlightenment.

events.text: A child climbs your mountain in winter, alone, and refuses to leave without learning one thing from you.

effects.log: Seven years. When they leave, they carry everything you know down the mountain. You feel lighter, and very proud.
One breath, taught perfectly. It is enough for a lifetime, and they know it.

events.text: In every teahouse, people argue over the Ten Greatest Masters Under Heaven, and now and then someone says your name.

effects.log: Half of what they say about you is wrong. The other half is flattering. (See the Ten Greatest in the Jianghu.)
Nobody believes you are you. You pay for their tea anyway.

events.text: The First Under Heaven sends you a single line of calligraphy: 'I am waiting.'

effects.log: Every morning you read it before training. It is better than any master.
The whole murim hears about it within a month.

events.text: Someone outside the Ten Greatest wants to be inside it, and has decided an ambush is quicker than a challenge.

ok.log: They chose the wrong night and the wrong master. Nobody tries that again for a while.

fail.log: You escape with a wound and a name. They will not be so lucky next time.
fail.deathCause: an ambush by a would-be master of the list

effects.log: You are not here to prove anything to people who fight like that.

events.text: A landslide has opened a cliff face no one has seen for centuries. Carved into the rock, stroke after stroke, is a single enormous sabre cut, and around it, smaller cuts that explain it.

ok.log: Forty days on the cliff. On the forty-first, your own sabre answers the stone. The Sabre That Splits the Sky is yours.

fail.log: The cuts make your head ache and your hands bleed. You understand a little. Perhaps the cliff will still be here in ten years.

choices.text: Copy it for the Martial Alliance

effects.log: The Alliance posts guards on the cliff. Your name is carved beside the sabre cut.

events.text: In a mountain pass, a rusted spear stands upright in the rock where a general once held the road alone for nine days. The villagers say it chooses who may pull it out.

ok.log: The rust falls away like old skin. Wrapped around the shaft, a silk scroll: the Nine Dragons Spear.

fail.log: It does not move. Your shoulder does, painfully. The villagers are very polite about it.

choices.text: Bow to the general and leave it

effects.log: Some things should stay where they are. The wind in the pass sounds almost grateful.

events.text: Floodwater has opened a sealed tomb in the hillside. Inside there is no coffin, only a sword laid across a stone table, and a single long cut across the ceiling, as if the sky above the tomb had been split and mended.

choices.text: Sit under the cut until it speaks

ok.log: For thirty days you watch the cut in the ceiling. On the thirty-first you understand it was not made by a sword swung at the stone, but by a sword swung at the sky. The Heaven-Splitting Sword is yours.

fail.log: The cut will not open for you. You leave with a headache and the feeling of having been politely refused.

effects.log: Whoever left the cut chose not to teach it to the living. You put the stones back the way they were.
